meeting_header:
Date: 2025-11-12 | Time: 15:00 - 15:50 UTC | Duration: 50 minutes
Attendees: Carlos Vega (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (CTO, Lakeside Health), Tina Moore (SecOps), Liam Chen (Data Eng)
summary: POC scoping call focused on security/compliance requirements for pilot: SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS. Discussed workload sizing, success criteria (latency/throughput/quality), benchmarks, timeline for a 4-6 week pilot. topics: Pilot success criteria: latency, throughput, accuracy/regression metrics
Benchmarks: baseline, metrics to capture (95th p95 latency, throughput, cost)
Security/compliance: SOC2, ISO 27001, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS/HSM, data residency
Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC
transcript:
[00:00] Carlos (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intro - I'm Carlos Vega, AE at Redwood; Maya is our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Raj (CTO): Hey Carlos, Raj here. Tina and Liam from my team are on.
[00:12] Maya (SE): hi all, quick agenda - confirm success criteria, walk through the security checklist for the pilot, agree on sandbox sizing and benchmark plan.
[00:22] Raj: sounds good. high level: Lakeside wants to run a 4-6 week pilot for a clinical triage assistant. Primary concerns are PHI handling, auditability, and SSO.
[00:33] Tina (SecOps): yes, SOC 2 compliance and ISO are table stakes. we need to see audit logs, retention policies, and encryption key controls (KMS/HSM). also SAML SSO + RBAC so we can map roles.
[00:45] Carlos: understood. we are SOC 2 Type II and we have ISO 27001 certs - i'll send the certs after the call. we also support customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM integrations for private deployments.
[00:58] Liam: for the pilot workload, rough numbers: we expect about 50 requests/sec peak, average 15 req/s, around 10M tokens/day with median prompt length ~220 tokens. this is for inference only, not training.
[01:15] Maya: thanks Liam, those numbers help. for sizing the dedicated sandbox we'll configure GPU-backed nodes to hit ~100 concurrent openai-style sessions; we usually target a 95th percentile latency below 200-250ms for short prompts but depends on model.
[01:32] Raj: latency target is 250ms p95. cost is also a factor — we'd like to measure unit cost per 1M tokens.
[01:40] Carlos: perfectly reasonable. success criteria suggestion: 1) functional parity vs baseline (we'll run evaluation prompts), 2) latency p95 <= 250ms, 3) sustain 50 req/s for 1 hour with burst to 80, 4) acceptable cost per 1M tokens, and 5) logs/auditability validated.
[01:58] Tina: on audit logs — we need immutable logs of requests/responses (redacted PHI), authentication events, admin actions, and ability to export logs to our SIEM. retention needs: 1 year online, archive to cold storage 7 years.
[02:18] Maya: Redwood supports request-level audit logs and can stream logs to customer endpoints (S3/CloudWatch). long-term retention can be handled with our archive options, or you can pull and store in your own bucket.
[02:33] Carlos: note that full request/response logging with PHI is sensitive; we recommend token-level redaction before persisting. we can help with a redaction pipeline as part of the pilot.
[02:46] Liam: good. about SSO — we run Okta and need SAML 2.0 integration and SCIM for provisioning. can you do automatic user sync and RBAC mapping?
[02:58] Maya: yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC mapping is supported; we expose roles and can sync groups via SCIM. there may be some small mapping work for custom roles.
[03:14] Raj: what about private deployment? we might prefer a VPC/private deployment for PHI. we need to know the difference between dedicated and private from a security perspective.
[03:25] Carlos: good question. Dedicated is isolated GPU pools within Redwood's infra with tenant isolation, SLA, and predictable throughput. Private is a customer-controlled VPC with a private control plane and optional on-prem connectors; it provides maximum isolation and is preferred for regulated PHI workloads. both support KMS but Private gives you full network control.
[03:46] Tina: so for pilot, can we start on Dedicated sandbox and later move to Private if post-pilot we go to production?
[03:53] Maya: yes, that's a common pattern. we can run the pilot on a dedicated sandbox with strict network egress rules and KMS, and then migrate to Private for production.
[04:04] Raj: benchmarks — what does Redwood capture by default? p95 latency, p50, throughput, error rates?
[04:12] Maya: we capture latency percentiles, token throughput, per-model breakdowns, error rates, and token-level cost metrics. we can also run our optimized batching and KV cache settings for better unit cost.
[04:25] Liam: for the benchmark, we want realistic concurrency and prefix caching behavior — our app often reuses context across session so cache hits matter.
[04:34] Maya: we'll run two benchmark passes: cold-cache and warm-cache. cold to measure raw model latency; warm to measure steady-state with KV/prefix caching. we'll share the benchmark template.
[04:47] Raj: timeline — we want pilot kickoff by end of November and run ~4 weeks. is that feasible?
[04:55] Carlos: yes. proposed timeline: week 1 - provisioning and security docs exchange; week 2 - baseline benchmark; week 3 - iterate on prompts and tuning; week 4 - validation and exec review.
[05:08] Tina: who owns the security review? we will need an NDA addendum and access matrix.
[05:15] Carlos: i'll route legal for the NDA addendum. for access matrix, we can provide SCIM role templates and RBAC docs.
[05:23] Maya: small note on encryption at rest — for Dedicated we offer platform-managed keys by default but can enable customer-managed KMS. for Private you control keys.
[05:34] Raj: what about auditability for admin actions? we need to see who changed model versions, who triggered rollouts, and token consumption reports.
[05:43] Maya: our console includes activity logs for config changes, rollout events, and per-token billing. we can grant read-only views via RBAC to your auditors.
[05:54] Liam: any gotchas with PHI and transcript retention? some vendors claim they don't retain data but logs show metadata retention.
[06:02] Carlos: we have clear data retention policies; by default we don't use customer data to train models and we provide options to entirely disable retention. we'll share the data processing addendum.
[06:13] Raj: ok, testing approach — we want a pass/fail matrix: 1) security controls validated, 2) perf within targets, 3) no regression in NLU accuracy.
[06:23] Maya: for accuracy, we'll run a curated eval set of ~1k prompts; measure F1/precision where applicable and human qualitative checks. we'll log outputs and provide diff reports versus your baseline.
[06:36] Tina: one more: can we run penetration testing on the sandbox?
[06:41] Carlos: yes, we allow pentests under scope with prior notice; we'll route the process and requirements.
[06:49] Raj: any competitors we should be aware of for this pilot? we've looked at OpenAI and Anthropic; cost/perf tradeoffs matter.
[06:58] Maya: noted — we can include side-by-side benchmarks if you want but first we'll get a baseline on Redwood.
[07:06] Carlos: recap of next steps: i'll send certs/DPAs/ISO docs; Maya will provision sandbox and run initial benchmark; Liam will share dataset and Tina will share compliance control list.
[07:20] Raj: that works. thanks everyone.
[07:24] Carlos: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for provisioning and the benchmark run.
[07:30] (call ends)
